label: Egyptian buffalo

names.text: 'Masri' is the alternate name given in the list's Egyptian entry, read on WebFetch. 'Baladi' is not on that page. It is found in the text of a WebSearch result (a review of Egyptian buffalo, not opened), which says the most common local name is Baladi.

about.text: The Egyptian buffalo is a river-type water buffalo kept in Egypt. It is divided into the long-horned milking Baladi of the Nile Delta, and the short-horned, mainly draught Saidi of Upper Egypt. It is kept for dairy and draught work.

sources.text: The list's Egyptian entry, read on WebFetch: river type, the Delta and Upper Egypt division into Baladi and Saidi, and the uses dairy and draught.

origin.place: Egypt, with its milking type in the Nile Delta and its draught type in Upper Egypt.

sources.text: The list's Egyptian entry, read on WebFetch. It gives no formation dates.
The list's Egyptian entry, read on WebFetch: use given as dairy and draught.

gaps: Searched for a DAD-IS risk status, a breed population with its year, and breed-specific milk yield, lactation length, fat and protein. None was found in pages opened. The Wikipedia article 'Egyptian buffalo' returned 404. The WebSearch text gave national figures (about 1,600 kg of milk per lactation nationally; lactations of 210 to 280 days) and a herd study of mean fat 7.68% at a Kafr El-Sheikh farm (2000 to 2007). These are not breed-specific and their pages were not opened, so they are left out. Egypt's total buffalo count (about 5.3 million in 2011, per the same search text) covers all buffaloes, not this breed, so it is left out. No formation dates.
